host_contention.note: calibration = wall ms of a fixed awk loop inside the VM; physical_host_load1 = 1-minute load average of the machine running the VM, sampled outside the VM when provided (physical-host-load.tsv)

rules: nearest-rank percentiles over all attempts of a group including failures; timing percentiles over attempts carrying the timing (n shown); nothing dropped

rfc_targets.target: cold first response: small Rust function, image cache hit, p95 <= 3 s (RFC §19)
rfc_targets.reason: p95 above 3000 ms on this host; see environment_boot_ms and the cgroup throttling ratio for where the time goes

rfc_targets.target: cold first response, image cache miss: reported separately (RFC §19)
rfc_targets.reason: RFC gives no number for the miss case; recorded so it is not mixed into the hit percentiles

rfc_targets.target: warm platform added latency p95 <= 20 ms, user handler excluded (RFC §19)
rfc_targets.reason: judged per sample on host_platform p95; host_platform = total_ms - handler_ms (queue, resume, readiness, response, bookkeeping) over every attempt of the warm group including any that fell back to cold; client_platform adds loopback HTTP and curl. RFC asks for same-region under a set load; this is loopback on one nested host, sequential

rfc_targets.target: Fast Restore: end-to-end p95/p99 and cost better than cold (RFC §19)
rfc_targets.reason: snapshot restore is not implemented (Capabilities.snapshot_clone = unsupported); X1 adds it to this benchmark
a few hundred requests on one host are not an availability measurement; failure rates are listed for the record only
